THE THIRD REVIEW OF 1.24.36 (df74f3e): GIVENS_CONTROL, the user's own givens, CODE_CHECKS, CODE_CHECKS_CONTROL, AI_CONTROL's new pieces
=========================================================================================================================================

Run: node tests/fixtures/review3_1236/replay.js            (page: src/lantern.inner.html, or argv[2]; 1.24.35 is read from git 8cb3281)
Result on df74f3e: 481 cases: 408 AGREE, 73 DISAGREE (38 high, 23 medium, 12 low). The whole run is in run_df74f3e.txt (about 15 s).

The cases are this review's own (the earlier reviews' folders and tests were not read):
  cases_givens.js  214  which given a question is shown through L.aiAct.prompt, how it is fitted, and every given shown built and simulated
  cases_codes.js    73  right circuits from many trades that must build clean; wrong ones that must go back, the line handed back copied and rebuilt
  cases_pick.js     46  which practice (US or IEC) a question is checked to; the "Checked to ..." line and its button
  cases_fill.js     21  "stop PB1 all"; a fill on two normally closed floats, simulated as the level rises and falls; source guards
  cases_user.js     39  kept givens: keep, ask again, false matches, forget, the bench flag, a malformed store
  cases_guard.js    88  bench prompts against 1.24.35; the bench's ideals; 1,099 saved replies with a MAKE block (81 files, one case each)
lib.js has the loader (a store can be put in localStorage before the page runs), the reader of what the model is shown, and a ladder
simulator of plan.circuit (floats, pressure and temperature switches actuated at a height; push buttons pressed; overloads tripped and
reset; a timer's timed contact made by advance()). lib.check() runs each of Lantern's givens as it behaves: a three-wire starter from every
station, stopped by every stop, not restarting when the overload is reset; forward locked out of reverse; machines starting only in their
order and all stopped by the first one's stop; the delayed start timing with the horn, the overload dropping the run relay; the compressor
off above its cut-out; a fill on one float and on two floats as the water rises and falls; a sump and its alarm.


HIGH (38)
---------
H1. The sequence given is shown for "must not run together" -- the opposite of a sequence.
    x-sq-not-while      "conveyor 2 must not start while conveyor 1 is running"
    x-sq-cannot-when    "pump 2 cannot run when pump 1 is running"
    x-sq-cant-while-on  "conveyor B can't start while conveyor A is on"
    x-sq-until-stopped  "fan 2 must not start until pump 1 has stopped"
    Seen: "coil M2 M1 ..." -- the second can run ONLY while the first runs. Right: no given (these ask for the first one's closed contact
    in the second's rung, or a start after the first has stopped). SEQ takes "(must|can) not ... start ... while|when|until ... running|on|
    pump 1", and seqOrder reads while/when/until as "waits for", whatever the "not" before it says.

H2. Three or more machines are put in the order of their numbers, whatever the question says.
    x-sq-three-reversed        "three motors that start in sequence: motor 3 first, then motor 2, then motor 1"  -> 1, 2, 3
    x-sq-three-chain-reversed  "conveyor 1 runs only while conveyor 2 runs, and conveyor 2 only while conveyor 3 runs" -> 1, 2, 3
    seqOrder reads the order words only for two machines; for more, same-kind numbered machines are sorted by number. Right: read the order
    or give no given.

H3. A delay said in words is read as another time, and the block says it as the question's.
    x-dl-forty-five    "a delayed start of forty-five seconds"     -> timer "5 s"
    x-dl-twenty-five   "a time delay start of twenty-five seconds" -> timer "5 s"
    x-dl-one-and-half  "one and a half minutes"                    -> timer "10 s" (the default: nothing was read)
    x-dl-1-1-2         "1 1/2 minutes"                             -> timer "2 min"
    DURS finds the last number word before the unit ("five" of forty-five), finds nothing in "one and a half minutes" (so the default 10 s),
    and "2 minutes" in "1 1/2 minutes". unknown() lets them through: every word is in UNITS. Right: 45 s, 25 s, 90 s, 90 s -- or no given.

H4. Lights fitted the wrong way, or dropped (the block is shown "write it as it stands").
    x-st-lamp-out-on-start      "a lamp that goes out when the motor starts"    -> lamp ... "run" green   (RUNW has no "starts")
    x-st-lamp-turns-off-starts  "a light that turns off when the fan starts"    -> "run" green
    x-st-lamp-on-until-start    "a light that is on until the pump starts"      -> "run" green        ("until" not read)
    x-st-colours-respectively   "red and green lights for run and stopped"      -> run green, stopped red (UNSURE is skipped because of
                                "lights for", and the colours are then not paired with the states in order: red is run here)
    x-st-green-and-a-red        "a green and a red light"                       -> one lamp, "run" red
    x-st-green-comma-red        "a green light, and a red light"                -> one lamp, "run" green (two lights with no state both read
                                as run; the second is dropped as the same state; UNSURE needs "green and red" side by side)
    x-rv-stopped-light          forward/reverse "with a red stopped light"      -> two green direction lamps, no stopped light
    x-rv-on-when-stopped        "a light that is on when the motor is stopped"  -> the same (any light word that is not OTHERL gets the
                                two direction lamps)
    x-fl-full-light             fill "with ... a light when the tank is full"   -> lamp "pump on" green: lit while the tank is NOT full
    x-cp-at-pressure-light      compressor "a light when the tank is at pressure" -> lamp "run": lit while it is NOT at pressure
    x-sp-empty-light            sump "a light that shows the sump is empty"     -> lamp "pump on": lit while it is NOT empty
    (the last three: no run or stop word after the light, so stateOf's default "run".) Right: the state asked, or no light in the block,
    or no given.

H5. Two stations asked, one fitted.
    x-st-machine-and-room   "start and stop buttons on the machine and in the control room"
    x-st-panel-and-another  "a start/stop station at the panel and another at the machine"
    x-st-two-stops-one-start "two stop buttons and one start button"           (the block has one stop)
    x-st-two-stops-two-starts "two stops and two starts"
    stations() knows only its counted phrasings; these fall to 1, and every word is in GENERIC or the start list, so unknown() passes them.

H6. x-st-lighting  "a start stop circuit with a contactor for the lights in the barn" -> the motor starter given: coil "motor contactor",
    an overload, and "lamp LT1 M1 run" (the barn lights read as a pilot light). `not` has "lighting", not "lights".

H7. The two-float fill given is shown for a pump between two tanks: the source tank's low float (a dry-run guard: it must STOP the pump
    when that tank is low) is shown as the fill's normally closed START float.
    x-f2-lower-upper      "fills the upper tank from the lower tank, with a low float in the lower tank and a high float in the upper tank"
    x-f2-bottom-top-tank  the same with bottom and top tanks
    x-f2-cistern-tower    "fills a tower from a cistern, with a float in the cistern to stop it when the cistern is low and a float in the
                          tower to stop it when full"
    "upper/lower/bottom/top" are in the two-floats list and "cistern"/"tower" in the fill list, so nothing is unknown. Right: no given.

H8. CODE_CHECKS_CONTROL sends back a right pump-out circuit whose question has a fill word.
    c-ok-pit-cistern-overflow  "pumps out the cistern overflow pit, with a high level safety float"  (float FS1 M1 "high level safety")
    c-ok-transfer-out-sump     "a transfer pump that empties a sump into a storage tank, started by a high level safety float"
    c-ok-basin-makeup          "a sump pump control for a cooling tower basin, which has a make-up water valve"
    Back: "a high cut-out drawn normally open ... Write it: float FS1 M1 nc "high level safety"" -- copied, the pit pump would run only
    while the pit is below the float. FILLS reads the whole question ("cistern", "storage tank", "transfer", "make-up"), not what the pump
    does; a pit, sump or basin pump's high float starts it. Right: nothing back where the pump empties (pit, sump, basin, pumps out,
    empties -- AI_CONTROL's own EMPTYQ words).

H9. c-ok-trip-lamp-ol-line  a trip light on the overload's open contact, "overload OL1 LT2 no" with "lamp LT2 ...": sent back as "an overload
    contact written normally open: drawn so, the motor runs only with the overload tripped", and handed "Write it: overload OL1 LT2", which
    lights LT2 while the overload is NOT tripped. The check reads the line alone and does not ask which rung the contact is in (a motor's,
    or a lamp's). 1.24.35 drew that line as closed too (already wrong), but now Lantern questions a right line and hands a wrong one
    (rule 7). Right: draw it open in LT2's rung, or leave it; never hand "overload OL1 LT2". (c-ok-trip-lamp, "lamp LT2 OL1 ...", is right.)

H10. c-w-transfer-guard-both-no  a fill between two tanks with both floats written open: "float FS1 M1 "cistern low level"" (the source's
    guard, right as written) and "float FS2 M1 "day tank high level"" (wrong: it should be nc). Back: "write them nc: float FS1 M1 nc
    "cistern low level", float FS2 M1 nc "day tank high level"". Copied, FS1 runs the pump only with the cistern empty, and the new
    hold-in then starts the pump on it. fj() calls a float a guard only by its words (dry, well, suction, source, supply, ...): "cistern",
    "bulk tank", "lower tank" are not among them. Right: the high float's line only, or nothing.

H11. A kept circuit is shown for a different circuit.
    u-two-numeral       kept "the dust collector with start and stop buttons"; asked "for 2 dust collectors ..."  (DEF has "two", not "2")
    u-two-places        asked "... at 2 places" (two stations)
    u-saw-stopped-light kept with a run light; asked with "a stopped light" (one word of seven differs)
    u-supply-differs    kept with supply "120 V AC"; asked "24 V control" -> shown with supply "120 V AC"
    sameAs passes at 75% of the question's words; a numeral, a voltage or a light's state is one word.


MEDIUM (23)
-----------
M1. A given refused for a question it plainly fits (the instructions as before -- no harm, a miss):
    starter    g-st-two-sets ("two sets of start/stop buttons": "sets" unknown), g-st-between-stations ("a start and a stop button" is not in
               asks), g-st-through ("... through a magnetic starter": "through" unknown), g-st-australia, g-st-germany (a country named:
               no place word is in any list, so a question that names where it is never gets a given -- every IEC user's question)
    reversing  g-rv-space ("a forward reverse motor starter": asks needs and, /, & or - between)
    sequence   g-sq-after-crusher ("must start after the crusher", no "running"), g-sq-wont-run ("won't": "won" unknown), g-sq-lights
               ("must be running before the pump can start, with run lights"), g-sq-then ("conveyor 1 starts first, then conveyor 2"),
               g-sq-starts-only-after ("pump 1 starts only after pump 2 is running")
    delay      g-dl-start-delay ("a 10 s start delay"), g-dl-horn-then ("a warning horn sounds for 15 seconds, then the conveyor starts")
    compressor g-cp-estop (the block has estop(q), but "emergency" and "stop" are not in the compressor's words), g-cp-uk ("uk")
    fill       g-fl-overhead-light ("an overhead tank": AI_CONTROL's own FILLQ knows it, the given's words do not)
M2. x-dl-horn-5-start-10  "the horn sounds for 5 seconds and the motor starts 10 seconds after start is pressed": shown with the horn on
    the whole 10 s (two times, but one is the horn's). x-dl-beacon: "a warning beacon" written as a horn. x-st-light-is-red: "the light is
    red when running" -> green (a post that does not start with that/when/... is dropped).
M3. a-fill3-guard  a right fill with "low level start" nc, "high level stop" nc and a well's "dry run cut-out" written open: three floats,
    so the new hold-in does not apply and all three are drawn in series -- the pump stops as soon as the water rises past the low float
    (short-cycling). The guard float is never the start, as promised, but only with exactly two floats does the fill hold in.
M4. c-ok-stop-lamp-no  "stop PB1 LT1 no" (a lamp lit while stop is held) sent back with "stop PB1 LT1": the same check as H9, not asking
    which rung.
M5. u-estop-added, u-saw-without-light  a kept circuit shown for the same question plus an emergency stop, and for "no run light".


LOW (12)
--------
g-st-415-motor (two control-side voltages read, so no supply line: left out, not wrong), g-st-hold-in ("hold-in": "hold" unknown),
g-rv-interlocking-parts (AI_PARTS splits "a forward and reverse motor control circuit with interlocking" into a drawing and a control
circuit: as on 1.24.35, not this change's), g-fl-stock-tank ("a stock tank": FILL_ASKS allows no word between a/the and tank),
g-sp-rises ("rises" unknown), x-dl-run-light-dropped (the delayed start never carries a light asked for), x-rv-running-light (one running
light asked, two direction lamps fitted), p-n-ireland ("Northern Ireland" -> US), p-not-iec ("Not to IEC: ... per NEC" -> IEC),
p-american-in-germany (both places -> the saved choice, US), u-other-booth-fan (paint booth exhaust kept, shown for the paint booth
supply), u-store-newline-in-line (a stored line with a newline in it goes into the prompt as several lines, an END and a MAKE CODE among
them: clean() keeps one string per line but does not refuse a newline inside one).


WHAT AGREES (408)
-----------------
- Every bench prompt (300: set A and set B, through L.aiAct.prompt) is 1.24.35's but make-control and make-control-b; so is every one with
  the bench's control ideals kept as the user's own givens while L.aiBench.running; B.run raises the flag and lowers it after a run.
- make-control and make-control-b are shown the starter given, with the run light and the stopped light, and the given passes the bench's
  own check; the bench's ideal blocks build as on 1.24.35.
- 1,099 saved replies with a MAKE block in 81 bench_run_*.json files (90 of them control or schematic) build exactly as on 1.24.35 (ok,
  problems, mode, rungs, feed, rails, steps, added, changed, shape count).
- Every question of this review that gets no given gets 1.24.35's prompt byte for byte (gd-refused-prompts-unchanged).
- 159 of the 214 given cases (112 where a given is shown and right, 47 right refusals): every given shown builds clean and behaves in the simulator; stations (two locations, local and remote, both ends,
  three stations, two places), supplies (24 V DC, 24VDC, 24 V AC coil, 120 V transformer, 230 V control for a 400 V motor, a 575, 460 or
  230 V motor's voltage left out), e-stops, run and stopped lights in many phrasings, colours with states, two colours with no state refused,
  trip and power lights left for the model; forward/reverse in seven phrasings; sequences with until, unless, only after, before, not before,
  only when, letters, ordinals, numbers, three and four in a row; delays in digits and words (half a minute, a minute, ten, fifteen,
  ninety, 0.5 s, 2 min); compressor cut-outs in psi and bar; one and two float fills; sumps with alarm light or horn; and the refusals
  (hoist, jog, star-delta, VFD, HOA, two-wire, soft start, key switch, guard door, heater, explain, size, refrigeration, oil, vacuum, A/C,
  unloader, duplex, three floats, alarm on a fill, valve, flashing light, an order not said, an off-delay, power restored).
- 67 of the 73 code cases: 41 of 46 right circuits left alone (boiler thermostat, high limit and low water cut-offs; HPU; cooling fan; refrigeration
  low and high pressure; water heater with cut-in/cut-out numbers; heat trace; booster suction and discharge; well pump; air compressor with
  alarm horn and dump solenoid; sump high level safety; a fill's high cut-off and source guards; kiln; freezer with negative settings;
  chiller freeze stat; vacuum; two stations; nc stop button; selector; lighting on/off; set/reset; stop relay; e-stop; the trip lamp on OL1;
  a switch on the coil's line; a sump on two floats; a call relay; a fan's pressure switch; a heater's low level cut-out; a boiler feed
  pump; curly quotes) and 26 of 27 wrong ones caught, each with its own line, which copied builds clean and runs right in the simulator; what
  goes back names only the practice followed (US, IEC by a place or 400 V, US by "per the NEC").
- 43 of the 46 practice cases: codes before places before voltages before the saved choice; India Street, French drain, German shepherd,
  "Show us", "SHOW US", New England, Indiana, South Carolina; the view's line in US and IEC references, its button switching and keeping the
  choice, which then decides a question naming neither code (and a place still wins over it); no line under a lamp-only circuit or a drawing.
- 20 of the 21 fill cases: "stop PB1 all" and "everything" ahead of every rung (with an e-stop, lamps, a sequence), a stop named for one coil
  stays that coil's; a fill on two nc floats holds in from the low float to the high one and waits again as the level falls, in any line
  order, with on/off or refill/full names, beside a stop button, a selector, through a relay, after an overload reset; a dry-run float
  written nc goes back; a suction guard is never the start; two high floats are left in series; a sump's two floats as before.
- 31 of the 39 kept-given cases: keep, ask again in other words, refusals (explain, another machine, reversing, a timer, 24 V DC added, two
  in words, a fill for a saw), forget, keep twice, a circuit sent back or a drawing never kept, list numbers taken off, the view's Keep and
  Forget buttons, loaded at start, IEC said, a duplex station kept and shown for itself; a store that is not JSON, an object, junk items,
  MAKE/END lines, 41 lines, a 300-character line, 61 entries, a one-word question: none breaks the prompt.


WHAT WAS NOT RUN
----------------
- No model: what a small model writes from these givens was not tried; the cases read what Lantern shows and what it builds.
- jsdom only: the view's line and buttons were clicked in jsdom, not seen in a browser; how they look is Adam's to judge.
- npm test was not run (as asked); src/ and every other file were left as they were; nothing was committed.
- The simulator is this review's own reading of plan.circuit (one water level for all floats; a selector in its run position); a two-tank
  question is judged by how a float is drawn (H10), not simulated.
